description:
FILED s473t2 (Opus triage of the 152 causeless blessed sweep rows), on main 0d783d24.
Source: perl-tests/blocks.t 190-256.

ROWS BEHIND IT: perl-tests/blocks.t 13 ("BEGIN{die} should exit"), 15
("UNITCHECK{die}"), 17 ("CHECK{die}"), 20 ("INIT{die}"), 26 ("GH Issue #16300:
Module::Install::DSL workaround") = 5 rows.

THE PROGRAM (blocks.t's $testblocks, one line):
    BEGIN { $| = 1; } BEGIN { print "begin\n"; } UNITCHECK { print "unitcheck\n"; }
    CHECK { print "check\n"; } INIT { print "init\n"; } END { print "end\n"; }
    print "main\n";
plus one extra `BEGIN { die; }`.

perl:  begin / Died at - line 1. / BEGIN failed--compilation aborted at - line 1. /
       unitcheck / check / end
PCL :  begin end Died at - line 1.
i.e. PCL aborts at the die and runs ONLY END; perl still runs the UNITCHECK and
CHECK blocks that were already queued, and prints the "<PHASE> failed" line.
The `exit 0` / `exit 1` siblings of these rows (12, 14, 16, 18, 19) PASS, so the
phase machinery itself is right -- only the die path is not.

Row 26 is the same family's diagnostic: perl prints
  Treating Module::Install::DSL::INIT block as BEGIN block as workaround at (eval 1) line 1.
before running the block; PCL runs the block ("INIT fired in eval") and prints
nothing.  That is a MANDATORY warning, not a warnings-gated one, so it is not
#221.
subject: BUG: a `die` inside BEGIN / UNITCHECK / CHECK / INIT stops the whole phase sequence -- perl runs the remaining QUEUED phase blocks and prints "<PHASE> failed--compilation aborted" (perl-tests/blocks.t, 5 blessed rows)
